user.title: Battery Management
user.description: Pick the household grid-power sensor (+ = import, - = export) and how many battery units to coordinate. You can tune the control parameters later under Configure.

data_description.grid_power_sensor: The household meter this steers on. Positive must mean importing, negative exporting. Everything else is derived from this one reading.
data_description.unit_count: How many packs to coordinate. Each gets its own screen next.
data_description.bias: Aim for this much import instead of exactly zero, so a brief overshoot still exports nothing.
data_description.deadband: Ignore errors smaller than this, otherwise the packs chase every kettle. Costs a steady-state error of at most bias + deadband.
data_description.kp: How hard it corrects per tick: new setpoint = old + Kp x error. Higher reacts faster and overshoots sooner. 0.25 at 15 s is proven stable here.
data_description.interval: Seconds between decisions. Do not go below 15: the Modbus sensors lag 10-30 s, and at 10 s both packs wound up and discharged into an export.
data_description.min_output: Below this a pack does nothing useful, so small shares are consolidated onto one unit instead of leaving both idling. Measure it; 150 W is a guess.
data_description.unit_max: Hard ceiling per pack, needed because the target entity's own maximum is unreliable - one unit here reports 10000 for a 3500 W device.

unit_device.title: Battery unit {index} of {total}: pick the device
unit_device.description: Pick the Anker device for this unit and the next screen is filled in for you - you still get to check it. Leave it empty to select all six entities by hand.

data_description.device_id: Pick the device and the next screen is filled in for you, for review. Leave empty to choose all six entities by hand.

unit.title: Battery unit {index} of {total}
unit.description: Select the Modbus control entities for this Anker SOLIX Max AC unit. The two limit fields are optional and expect a percentage - leave them blank to use 100 % / 5 %.

data_description.name: Used in this integration's own sensor names. Must be unique: two packs sharing a name would be treated as one.
data_description.operating_mode_select: The select that switches this pack between its own control and being driven from outside. Which option means what is asked on the next screen.
data_description.grid_flow_select: The select that chooses charging or discharging. Must offer charge and discharge literally - those are written as-is.
data_description.target_power_number: The number this pack's share of the setpoint is written to. Always positive; the direction comes from the flow select.
data_description.soc_sensor: Drives the split between packs and every SoC limit. A pack whose state of charge cannot be read is skipped entirely.
data_description.charge_limit_number: The pack's own upper limit, as a percentage. Leave empty to assume 100 %. Never point this at a watt entity.
data_description.discharge_limit_number: The pack's own lower limit. Leave empty to assume 5 %. This is the hardware backstop the coordinator stays above.

unit_modes.title: Battery unit: {name} - what its modes mean
unit_modes.description:
This unit offers: {options}.

Pick which one hands control to the coordinator, and which one gives it back when you switch off. Leave the second empty if there is nothing to return to - the unit is then simply commanded 0 W, which is a safe resting state. A pack without its own P1 meter has no self-consumption mode, so this is normal.

data.mode_safe: Option to return to when switching off

data_description.mode_control: The option this pack must be set to before it will take orders. Usually third_party_control.
data_description.mode_safe: Where it is put when you switch off or Home Assistant unloads. Leave empty for a pack with no meter of its own: it is then simply commanded 0 W and its mode left alone, which is a safe resting state.

error.duplicate_name: Another unit already uses this name. Names must be unique, otherwise the two packs are treated as one.
error.duplicate_entity: This entity is already used for another field on this unit. Each field needs its own entity.
error.limit_not_percentage: This looks like a power entity, not a state-of-charge percentage. The limit fields expect a percentage (0-100); leave blank to use 100 % / 5 %.
error.missing_options: This select does not offer the options the coordinator needs (self_consumption / third_party_control, or charge / discharge). Check the entity, or adjust the option strings in const.py if your firmware renamed them.

tuning.title: Tune the coordinator
tuning.description: Saving reloads the integration. Each unit is briefly released as far as it can be, then the coordinator resumes on its own with the setpoint it had.

data.fast_charge_hold: Keep the packs full after a fast charge
data.full_charge_minutes: Minutes from empty to full at max power
data.external_timeout: Minutes an external setpoint stays valid

data_description.fast_charge_hold: On: the switch stays on at full and holds them there until you release it. Off: it switches itself off and your mode discharges them again.

data_description.external_timeout: In External plan mode: if no new plan arrives within this time, control returns to following the meter instead of freezing on the last instruction.

dynamic.title: Dynamic tariff
dynamic.description: Optional. Without a price sensor the Dynamic mode is not offered and nothing else changes. Exchange (day-ahead) prices are enough: tax and markup shift every hour equally, so the cheap-to-expensive order is the same.

data.cheap_hours: Hours a day to buy on
data.charge_below_soc: Only buy below this state of charge (%)
data.solar_forecast_max: Fallback: skip buying above this many kWh expected
data.expensive_hours: Hours a day to save the charge for

data_description.price_sensor: Any integration publishing upcoming prices. Exchange prices are enough: tax and markup shift every hour equally, so the cheap-to-expensive order is unchanged. Without one, Dynamic mode is not offered.
data_description.cheap_hours: How many of the coming day's cheapest slots may be used to charge from the grid. Ranked over a rolling 24 hours, not over everything published.
data_description.charge_below_soc: Fallback ceiling, used only while the charge time is unmeasured. Once it is, the solar-aware ceiling replaces it.
data_description.solar_forecast_max: Only used while the charge time is unmeasured, since without a capacity there is no way to turn kWh into a percentage. 0 ignores the forecast.
data_description.expensive_hours: Outside the dearest hours the packs do not discharge, so a cheap hour is bought from the grid and the stored kWh go to the peak instead. 0 switches this off.
data_description.discharge_anyway_soc: A pack this full discharges even during a cheap hour. Refusing would leave nowhere for the sun still coming, and spilling free energy to save a few cents is a bad trade.
data_description.solar_forecast_sensors: Pick every roof plane; they are summed. Prefer the 'remaining today' variants - a whole-day total is right at 02:00 and wrong at 17:00.
data_description.solar_produced_sensor: Only needed if the sensors above give a day total: this is subtracted, leaving what is still to come.

shadow.title: Shadow running
shadow.description: Only matters while Dry run is on. Simulating the meter is what makes a shadow comparison honest: without it the other controller is already regulating the meter, so this one sees nothing to do and parks at zero.

data.shadow_simulate: Simulate the meter from reconstructed demand

data_description.shadow_simulate: Only matters in dry run. Without it the other controller is already regulating the meter, so this one sees nothing to do and parks at zero - comparing the old system with itself.
data_description.battery_power_sensor: Signed, + discharging, for both packs together. Leave empty and it is read back from the target entities, where the other controller writes. Never the grid meter: the reconstruction adds the two together.

error.battery_power_is_grid: That is the grid meter, not the batteries. The reconstruction adds the two together, so using the meter here counts it twice and the comparison becomes worthless. Leave this empty unless you have a sensor for the packs' own combined power - empty reads it back from the target entities, which is what you want.

state.external_stale: External plan went quiet, regulating on its own
state.dynamic_hold: Holding the charge for dearer hours

external_no_plan.title: Smart charging needs an external optimiser
external_no_plan.description:
The coordinator is set to **External plan**, but no plan has arrived in the last {timeout} minutes, so it has handed control back to normal grid-zero regulation.

This mode does not plan anything itself. It executes a plan produced elsewhere — typically **EMHASS**, which optimises against price, solar and load forecasts. EMHASS is a separate project: it is **not** installed with this integration and is not a dependency.

Install and configure it (or any other optimiser), and have it call the `battery_management.set_setpoint` service. Positive discharges, negative charges. This message clears itself as soon as a plan arrives.

Not using an optimiser? Pick a different mode — **Follow the meter** charges from your solar surplus and discharges on demand, with no extra software.
